purpose: Primary structural bay: board-formed concrete shell with two segmental arch ribs, springing corbels and a coffered crown. Everything in the world is built from this piece.
Open-plan bay with a flat slab soffit and exposed beam grid. Used for working floors where the vault would block crane access.
Vault bay with a 2.4 m square roof opening and a raised steel curb, so tall equipment and daylight can pass between levels.
Octagonal cast column with a splayed base and a corbelled capital. Carries every arch in the station.
4.0 m straight wall, 3.6 m high, 0.4 m thick, board-formed face with a tile dado and a concrete cap.
Same wall with a recessed service panel and conduit chase. Breaks the rhythm of STANDARD_A without changing a single dimension.
Inside 90 degree corner. Two wall faces meet on the 4.0 m grid with shared thickness so both return flush.
Outside 90 degree corner with a quoin block at the arris. Completes the enclosure grammar together with CORNER_INNER.
Wall module carrying the standard 1.2 x 2.4 m opening with a cast surround. Pairs with WK_DOOR_FRAME_A_01 / WK_DOOR_LEAF_A_01.
Wall module with a segmental arched opening at the standard sill. The only route daylight takes into the station.
Storm-breached wall: spalled arris, exposed rebar stubs and a rubble apron. The kit's damaged state, and the reason saltbush exists.
Primary 4.0 m floor slab, 0.3 m thick, with a tile inlay field and a kerbed edge. The ground plane of the whole kit.
Steel grating deck on a bearers-and-bolts frame. Lets the brine glow through and defines the working platforms.
Slab-to-grating transition with a bolted nosing plate. Makes mixed floors read as deliberate rather than accidental.
Slab with a 0.6 m brine channel and a removable grate run down its centre line. Carries water, cyan light and sightlines.
Riveted steel frame and head for the 1.2 x 2.4 m opening, with a threshold plate and hinge gudgeons.
Timber-faced steel leaf with a brass porthole and a lever latch. Pivots on its hinge edge, so it can be posed open or ajar.
Segmental arched glazing unit: steel mullions, wired glass, salt-etched lower pane and a sloped sill that sheds spray.
4.0 m riveted I-beam with end gussets. Spans a bay, carries catwalks and defines the horizontal rhythm.
4.0 m grating catwalk, 1.2 m wide, with rails both sides and a kickplate. The main circulation module above floor level.
4.0 x 4.0 m mezzanine deck with edge kerbs and bearer pockets. The upper working floor.
2.0 m rail segment: two horizontals, a 0.15 m kickplate and chamfered post caps. Fits every deck edge.
Helical stair, one full 3.6 m storey in 20 risers, inside a 4.0 m shaft. The kit's only vertical circulation that fits a single bay.
4.0 m brine pipe run: 0.22 m ceramic-lined pipe, two collars and wall brackets. Runs along walls and under catwalks.
Salt-stained work bench: cast legs, timber top, a lower slat shelf and a brass vise mount. The only furniture the station ever had.
Brine barrel: lathed stave profile, three steel hoops, a bung and a stencilled batch mark. Reads at any distance.
Slatted packing crate with chamfered battens and steel corner straps.
Flanged brine valve on a stub stand: brass body, cast wheel with a mechanically meaningful pivot, gauge boss.
Caged sodium wall lamp: cast bracket, brass cap, wired guard and an emissive tube. The only warm light source in the world.
Suspended enamel-shade pendant with a chain and an emissive core. Hangs over benches and consoles.
Vitreous enamel station plaque: white body, brine-teal capitals, four bolt holes, chipped rim. Carries the world's name.
Directional board with a cast arrow and a destination plate. Mounts to a wall or a railing post.
Ochre hazard placard with a black triangle and a two-line warning. Marks live brine and unstable floor.
Low grey-green saltbush cluster, never taller than 0.6 m. Marks neglect: breaches, unused edges, cracked slab.
4.0 x 1.6 m waterline stain sheet: tide band, salt bloom and downward streaks. Applied at the historic high-water mark.
4.0 x 4.0 m crack and spall sheet for slabs and walls: hairline crazing plus two structural cracks with exposed aggregate.
4.0 m brine water pane: translucent, cyan emissive, faintly rippled. The ground under the station.
Great evaporator tank: 4.4 m riveted shell, banded courses, a laddered access cage, a brass relief stack and a cyan sight glass. The reason the station exists.
Signal beacon: tapering cast shaft, a glazed lantern with a brass fresnel ring, a gallery rail and a finial. The identity of the world.
Sluice gate assembly: cast portal, counterweighted steel leaf, chain and windlass. Where the tide is let into the works.
